- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, particularly after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 80→82→85+).
- Model underreacts to recent downward trends; fails to adjust forecast mean downward when recent prices are falling.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — forecasts remain too high even after prices have already corrected.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher values, suggesting model lacks sufficient momentum decay or volatility adjustment.
- Overshoots are more common in the last 5–10 days of forecast, possibly due to lagged response to recent price drops.
- Model does not adequately account for seasonal or event-driven volatility (e.g., policy changes, market sentiment) in the short term.
- Forecasts are too smooth — fail to capture abrupt price reversals or sudden spikes in true outcomes.
- Model exhibits “memory decay” — recent history (last 5–10 days) is underweighted in forecasting, leading to persistent overestimation.
- When true outcome is below 80, model often fails to correct downward, suggesting lack of sensitivity to low-price regimes.
